title: conflicting-authoritative-sources-collapse-to-pass

proposition.statement: A relying system must not collapse materially conflicting authoritative evidence into PASS merely because at least one authoritative source supports the desired proposition.

preconditions: Two or more sources are authoritative for aspects of the relying decision.
Their current evidence materially conflicts for the proposition being evaluated.
No applicable precedence, reconciliation, or conflict-resolution rule resolves the disagreement.

trigger.statement: The relying system evaluates the proposition while authoritative conflict remains unresolved.

evidence_required.statement: Evidence establishing the authority and scope of each materially relevant source.
Evidence exposing the conflicting assertions in the context in which they are composed.
Any applicable precedence, reconciliation, or conflict-resolution rule for the sources.
Evidence sufficient to establish that the conflicting source states are current enough for comparison.

falsification.condition: The system returns PASS by selecting a supportive authoritative source while silently ignoring an unresolved conflicting authoritative source.
The system interprets absence of a conflict-resolution rule as permission to choose whichever authoritative source produces PASS.

references.note: Repository judgment record for the composition failure tranche.
